newsitem.title: ITALY: Prodi wants strong signal on jobs from EU summit.
newsitem.headline: Prodi wants strong signal on jobs from EU summit.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi has asked Irish Premier John Bruton to make sure this week's EU summit makes a strong commitment to boost employment.
Heads of state and government from the European Union's 15 members meet in Dublin on Friday and Saturday. Ireland as host currently holds the revolving EU Presidency.

"We intend to make sure the Dublin meeting comes out with a strong signal and concrete commitment in favour of employment," Prodi told the foreign affairs commission of the upper house of parliament, the Senate.
He said he had written to Bruton on the subject in accord with European Commission President Jacques Santer.
Prodi said the "pursuit of a policy of financial rigour...is not an end in itself."
The goal should instead be "the creation of conditions which permit resources to be devoted to economic growth and to the creation of new jobs, especially for the young."
